assumptions.regular_long_wave_branch: |theta(tau,k)| <= C_theta k^2 and |B(tau,k)| <= C_B on the finite interval, with finite k-independent C_theta,C_B

proof: Integrate the exact identity: I_f-I_i=-integral_{tau_i}^{tau_f}(theta+k^2 B)d tau.
Therefore I_f/I_i -> 1 as k->0 on any fixed finite regular in-EFT interval.

theorem.limit: lim_{k->0} I_f/I_i = 1 for the stated nonzero regular family
theorem.no_uniform_finite_time_attractor: No regular finite-time in-EFT evolution satisfying the stated bounds can uniformly drive every O(1) nonzero initial neutral charge to zero as k->0.

relation_to_C10_62b.important_distinction: The frozen C10.62b diagnostic measures the largest singular value of Y=(delta_khr,theta_khr/k), not I_khr directly.
relation_to_C10_62b.consequence: Even if the Y-norm contracts at some finite positive k, that alone does not demonstrate erasure of the conserved/slow neutral charge, because I_khr=delta/(1+w)-3 psi_pref uses a time-dependent map from Y and metric variables.
relation_to_C10_62b.required_interpretation: Compare the retained/decaying C10.62b singular direction with I_khr and add a charge-aware transfer diagnostic before claiming physical memory loss.

physical_interpretation: The neutral shift charge is a boundary/charge datum that survives regular superhorizon finite-time evolution up to O(k^2) leakage. Cosmological initial-condition uniqueness therefore requires either a pre-EFT/UV prescription fixing the charge sector, sufficiently long k-dependent evolution, or a violation of the regularity assumptions; this theorem does not choose among them.
does_not_exclude: O(1) damping at fixed observational finite k
O(1) change over intervals Delta_tau scaling like k^-2 or faster
singular branches where theta/k^2 or B diverges as k->0
a UV/pre-EFT rule that fixes I_i, including potentially I_i=0
time-dependent contraction of the coordinate norm Y=(delta,theta/k)
additional coupled photon+baryon+UR effects at finite k
